# Provenance — public TonyPi Pro model (pab47/TonyPi)

- **Source:** https://github.com/pab47/TonyPi, files `LICENSE`, `model/robot.xml`, `model/scene.xml` and the 21 STL meshes in `model/assets/`
- **Commit:** `97807f5e26049ce1c3d90b1c80d5d2a92606d40f` (2026-09-24, "Add files via upload"). On 2026-11-19 it was still the head of `main`: GitHub's compare API reported `identical`, with no newer commits, tags or releases. The model files last changed in `8b4cf1a5` ("updated all model files", 2026-09-24).
- **Authors and licence:** MIT License, "Copyright (c) 2026 Pranav Bhounsule". A verbatim copy is in `LICENSE`. The upstream README says Salvador Echeveste built the XML model from a STEP (.stp) file that Hiwonder provided. `robot.xml` says it was generated by `tools/gen_mjcf.py` from `joints.json`, `link_inventory.json` and `inertia.json`; none of those generator inputs are in the upstream repository.
- **How this copy was obtained (2026-11-19):** the 24 files were copied from a local snapshot of the same commit already on this computer, not downloaded again. Every file was then checked against GitHub's tree for the pinned commit (`git/trees/97807f5…?recursive=1`, `truncated: false`): all 24 local git blob SHA-1s equal the upstream blob SHA-1s, so the bytes are identical to upstream.
- **Integrity:** `SHA256SUMS` lists the SHA-256 of the 24 files. From this folder: `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` (macOS) or `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` (Linux, Git Bash).
- **Not copied:** upstream also has `model/robot_mink.xml` and `scene_mink.xml` (an inverse-kinematics variant), `control/` (controllers, the hardware bridge and `servo_map.py`), and an `action/` folder with 118 Hiwonder `.d6a` action groups and Hiwonder's action-group list. The action groups are Hiwonder's stock motions. Hiwonder's own TonyPi repository has no licence, so they are not redistributed here. `model/servo_map.csv` cites the calibration numbers from `control/servo_map.py` instead of copying the file.

Do not edit files here. Corrections go into `model/ledger.csv`, and `model/build_twin.py` builds the twin from that ledger plus these files.

## What the upstream files say about themselves

These are upstream statements, recorded so that no vendor number is mistaken for a Hiwonder specification:

- **Masses:** there are no `<inertial>` elements. Link masses come from explicit box masses: 18 LX-824HV cases at 57 g, 2 LFD-01M cases at 14 g, battery 148 g, Raspberry Pi 5 46 g, expansion board 55 g, plus structure, fastener and sole boxes. They sum to 1.800002 kg; Hiwonder lists "about 1800 g". MuJoCo computes the inertias from those boxes.
- **Servo dynamics:** the bus-servo `armature` of 0.015 is labelled ESTIMATE ("Hiwonder does not publish the LX-824HV gear ratio"). The joint `damping` reproduces each servo's torque-speed line (stall torque divided by no-load speed). No basis is given for `frictionloss` or the head-servo armature.
- **Servo gains:** `kp` and `dampratio` are simulation choices. `kp="64"` on the four hip/ankle roll servos is a "ROLL-STIFFNESS FIX" tuned for simulated walking foot clearance.
- **Measured on the upstream author's robot:** the sole footprint (11 cm front to back) and a 2 cm inner gap between the feet in the stand pose, plus the servo-case orientations ("orientation MEASURED … from perpendicular bores"). The head-servo case orientation is labelled ESTIMATE. That robot had fixed hands, not the Pro's open/close hands ("the real hardware (no grippers, fixed hand)").

## Conventions and known inconsistencies

- **Frame:** metres, radians, +Z up. In the home pose the robot faces −Y. The Raspberry Pi, battery and expansion board sit at +Y, which is the robot's back. Bodies prefixed `l_` sit at +X, the robot's own left (right-handed axes with −Y forward and +Z up). The shoulder-pitch range also points the large arm swing toward −Y.
- **Mesh names are mirrored:** every `r_*` body uses an `l_*.stl` file and every `l_*` body an `r_*.stl` file. Follow each geom's `mesh` attribute and never infer a side from a file name.
- **Servo IDs in the XML comments are reversed:** the comments beside the body actuators put bus IDs 1–8 on `r_*` joints. Hiwonder's 20-DOF ID diagram, Hiwonder's stock action groups and the upstream executable simulator (`control/TonyPi_sw/tonypi_sim.py`) all put IDs 1–8 on the robot's left. `model/servo_map.csv` follows the diagram and the simulator. The hand comments (`l_gripper` "servo 17", `r_gripper` "servo 18") also disagree with Hiwonder's code, where the right hand is ID 17. The map uses 17 for the right hand and 18 for the left, and records the conflict.
- **Strict XML parsers:** some comments contain `--`, which ElementTree rejects. `tools/inspect_mjcf.py` strips comments in memory before parsing. The files on disk are never changed.
- **IMU axes:** the upstream simulator's IMU comment calls the site frame "+x right, +y back, +z up", which is a left-handed triad, so its mapping to the hardware IMU may carry one sign error. The twin exposes MuJoCo's IMU-site sensors in the torso frame and makes no claim about the MPU6050's mounting axes.
